fields.title: Why the response is different every time
fields.keyTakeaway: Response variance is a feature, not a defect, and the product must decide for each scenario whether it is acceptable or squelched by a strict format and code validation of the result.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: A QA engineer sent a bug: "the response is different the second time". Is this a defect?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: Non-determinism breaks familiar ways of working: testing, support, reproducing bugs. A team that hasn't adapted its processes wastes time on "bugs" that aren't bugs and misses real problems.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: At each step, the model outputs a probability distribution of the next [[token|token]]. Then [[sampling|sampling]] occurs—a selection from this distribution. [[temperature|Temperature]] controls diversity: lower means more probable choices, more stable responses; higher means more diverse.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: Even at zero temperature, complete reproducibility is not guaranteed: request batching, model version, and hardware specifics all have an effect.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: Product consequences, each requiring a decision:
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: **Testing changes.** You cannot compare against a standard character by character. What gets checked is not a match, but properties: is the required fact present, is the format followed, is there anything forbidden. Covered in `AI2-N4`.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: **Support changes.** "I got something different" is a normal message. To investigate, you need to store actual responses with an identifier.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: **Trust changes.** A person who sees two different answers to the same question starts doubting both. This is a product problem, and it is not solved by tech.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: **Where variance is acceptable and where it is not:**
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/rows/1/1: No, there must be a single fact
fields.sections/2/blocks/7/rows/3/1: Partially: the set can differ, quality cannot
fields.sections/2/blocks/8/text: For the second and third categories, techniques include: low temperature, strict output format, code verification of the result.
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: *Product answers.* Temperature is minimal, format is strict, facts are taken solely from context. Variance remains in phrasing, not content. A user who asks a question twice gets different words with the same meaning—this is acceptable.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: *Cart picking.* Temperature is medium. Different sets upon repeat are not a defect, but a feature. But we added a "different option" button that makes variance explicit and controllable instead of random.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: *Extracting ingredients from supplier descriptions.* Strict JSON format, zero temperature, result checked by code: if a field fails to parse, we retry once, then flag the item for manual processing.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: The last one is a general technique: **where reliability is needed, the model's result is verified by a program rather than taken on faith.**
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Low temperature does not eliminate errors, it makes them stable. The model will confidently repeat the same wrong answer.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Response variance is a feature, not a defect, and the product must decide for each scenario whether it is acceptable or squelched by a strict format and code validation of the result.
